headline: ARTEMIS GOLD ACQUIRES VISTA GOLD IN $427M ALL-STOCK DEAL — MT TODD ADDS AUSTRALIA GROWTH OPTION TO BLACKWATER
snippet: Artemis Gold Inc. agreed to acquire Vista Gold Corp. in an all-stock deal valued at $427 million (C$598 million), expanding beyond the Blackwater Gold Mine in British Columbia to add the Mt Todd gold project in Northern Territory, Australia. Vista Gold shareholders receive 0.0966 Artemis shares per share, representing a 29% premium to Vista's 20-day VWAP, with no cash consideration and no new debt. With Blackwater's EP2 expansion targeting mid-2028 completion, Mt Todd provides a long-dated growth option as Artemis builds toward multi-asset producer status at a time when deal premiums in the gold sector remain suppressed relative to gold's record price environment.

headline: DPM METALS DRILLS 716M AT 3.30 g/t AuEq AT BREVENE SOUTH — BULGARIA PORPHYRY OPEN AT DEPTH AND IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: DPM Metals Inc. (TSX: DPM) delivered expanded delineation results at the Brevene Porphyry South discovery in Bulgaria, with hole EXBRES55502A returning 716.60 metres at 3.30 g/t AuEq from 1,357m downhole and EXBRESPO_03 returning 1,054 metres at 2.49 g/t AuEq — both terminated in mineralization due to equipment limits, not geology. The potassic alteration envelope now exceeds 500 by 500 metres and over 1,000 metres vertically, with the system confirmed to extend onto the adjacent operating Chelopech mine concession. Up to 15,000 additional metres of drilling on Chelopech ground are planned through year-end 2026.

headline: MARATHON FULLY FUNDED AT C$1.3 BILLION — GENERATION MINING TO BREAK GROUND ON COPPER-PALLADIUM MINE IN Q4 2026
snippet: Generation Mining Ltd. has assembled the full C$1.3 billion construction financing package for the Marathon copper-palladium mine in northwestern Ontario, with early works expected to begin in Q4 2026. The package includes commitments from the Canada Growth Fund, Canada Infrastructure Bank, Wheaton Precious Metals, and Glencore — which also holds the copper concentrate offtake. Over a 13-year mine life, Marathon is forecast to produce 532 million pounds of copper, 2.16 million ounces of palladium, and 3.05 million ounces of silver, positioning it as Canada's first new palladium mine and a critical-minerals project of national strategic significance.

headline: JAPAN'S JX ADVANCED METALS FUNDS $700K KALI METALS LACHLAN BELT EXPLORATION — ZERO DILUTION FOR ASX:KM1 SHAREHOLDERS
snippet: Kali Metals Ltd. (ASX: KM1) signed a binding MOU with Japanese industrial giant JX Advanced Metals Corporation on September 22, 2026, under which JX will fund up to $700,000 in exploration across Kali's 1,413 km² Southern Lachlan Fold Belt project prospective for lithium-caesium-tantalum pegmatites, tin, and tungsten. Kali retains full operatorship and earns a management fee, advancing a major land position at zero cost to shareholders while preserving 100% ownership through a due diligence period running to March 31, 2027. A funded strategic partner from one of Japan's largest metals groups signals both project prospectivity and downstream industrial interest.

headline: CRITICAL MINERAL CHOKEHOLD SOFTENS TRUMP'S APPROACH BEFORE XI SUMMIT THURSDAY — RARE EARTHS RESHAPING US LEVERAGE
snippet: A Reuters analysis published September 21 documents how China's accumulated leverage over rare earth and critical mineral supply is moderating Trump's usual adversarial posture ahead of Thursday's White House summit with Xi Jinping — the administration has not threatened additional tariffs or technology bans in the pre-summit period as it did before prior meetings. Washington's stated concern is that China's delivery of rare earth magnets and critical minerals 'has not been up to par' since the Busan agreement, but structural dependence on Chinese materials — yttrium for turbine coatings, antimony for semiconductors, NdPr for defense magnets — limits the tools available for leverage until supply-chain alternatives outside China are established.

headline: TRUMP-XI SUMMIT THURSDAY: CRITICAL MINERALS, TARIFF TRUCE, AND COPPER FLOWS — WHAT MINING INVESTORS SHOULD WATCH
snippet: Thursday's White House summit between Trump and Xi carries the most direct commodity market implications of any bilateral meeting this year, with critical mineral deliveries, the November 10 tariff truce expiry, and AI guardrails on the agenda. For mining investors the key commodity reads are: antimony (at US record prices from Chinese export controls), copper (where tariff rhetoric has driven a $300–500/t binary in either direction), and rare earths (where a concrete Chinese delivery commitment would ease Greenland-proxy stocks sharply from Monday's speculative surge). Analysts expect incremental progress rather than a breakthrough, with gold and silver most sensitive to any unexpected geopolitical escalation.

headline: RUSSIA'S ACID BAN WON'T HIT KAZATOMPROM IN 2026 — BUT 2027 URANIUM SUPPLY IS NOW A STRUCTURAL RISK
snippet: Kazatomprom confirmed September 21 that Russian sulfuric acid suppliers will fulfill existing 2026 contractual obligations following Russia's September 12 government resolution restricting acid exports through December 31 — meaning 2026 uranium production guidance is intact. However, Kazatomprom requires approximately 1.5 million tonnes of externally sourced sulfuric acid annually, with Russia supplying 93.6% of Kazakhstan's acid imports, and 2027 negotiations are ongoing in an uncertain regulatory environment. Any sustained tightening of Russian acid availability would directly threaten Kazakhstan's output, which accounts for roughly 45% of global uranium production.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,377 ABOVE POST-HIKE FLOOR — SUMMIT THURSDAY IS THE KEY TO BREAKOUT ABOVE $4,430 RESISTANCE
snippet: Gold is trading near $4,377 per ounce ahead of Tuesday's session, having rebounded from the $4,235 post-Fed-hike low of last week in a move GoldSilver.com attributes to a decoupling of gold from real yields that has characterized the entire 2026 bull cycle. Key technical levels are $4,307 (primary support), $4,376 (immediate resistance), and $4,430 (the upper boundary of the multi-week horizontal channel) — with Thursday's Trump-Xi summit as the binary event that could accelerate a breakout on escalation risk or fade the safe-haven bid toward support on a cooperative critical minerals outcome. Silver is outperforming slightly at $67.30, compressing the gold-to-silver ratio.

headline: SEPTEMBER 2026 GOLD STOCK SCREEN: WHICH JUNIORS HAVE THE MOST LEVERAGE AT $4,377 GOLD — A FUNDAMENTALS VIEW
snippet: The Canadian Mining Report's September 2026 fundamentals screen of junior and mid-tier gold stocks identifies the most compelling names at record gold prices by focusing on balance-sheet quality, development milestones within 12 months, and resource scalability through active drill programs. At current prices above $4,300/oz, even development-stage projects modeled at $1,800/oz are generating triple-digit IRRs — but the challenge for retail investors is separating companies with genuine resource upside from those merely riding the gold tape. The screen flags several TSX and TSXV companies where the operational leverage story is backed by real near-term catalysts rather than speculative momentum.
